To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IL‐12Rbeta1 expression on Th17 cells is a better predictor of Th17 responsiveness to IL‐ 23 than the IL‐23 receptor expression, and IL‐23 receptor is expressed on human γδ T cells.
IL‐12R β‐1 subunit is a better predictor of the Th17 cells responsiveness to IL‐‐23 than IL‐23R, and IL‐23R is also expressed on γδ T lymphocytes.
Th17 cells express heterogeneous expression of the IL23R subunit, which is a less reliable indicator of responsiveness to IL23 than expression of the IL12Rβ1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression and function of the IL‐17/IL‐23 axis in human T cells.
the expression of IL‐23R by CD4 Th17 and γ δ T cells.
the development of new reagents and the application of these to understand the expression and function of IL‐23R on human Th17 cells and γδ cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IL‐23R is expressed on human Th17 cells but not on γδ T‐cells.
the IL‐12 receptor subunit β1, rather than IL‐23R, is a better marker for IL‐23 responsiveness of Th17 cells.
the IL‐23 receptor is expressed on human Th17 cells and γδ cells but is not required for IL‐23 responsiveness of Th17 cells and is only a partial requirement for the responsiveness of γδ cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IL‐23R is expressed by Th17 cells and γδ cells but that the IL‐12β1 subunit is a better indicator of responsiveness to IL23.
the IL‐12 receptor β1 subunit, not the IL‐23 receptor, is a major determinant of responsiveness to IL-23.
IL‐12R subunit expression is a better predictor of Th17 cell responsiveness than IL‐23R, and IL‐23R is not required for γδ T cell responsiveness to IL‐6 and IL‐23.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Th17 cells and γδ cells are distinct subsets that are both responsive to IL‐17.

the expression of IL‐12Rbeta1, a shared subunit of the IL‐6R, IL‐12R and IL‐23R, is a more sensitive predictor of responsiveness of T cells to IL‐23 compared to the expression of the unique IL‐23R chain, which is also a shared chain of the IL‐9 receptor.
the IL‐23‐responsive Th17 cells are a distinct subset within the Th17 cells and that the Th17 cells are not the only source of IL‐17.
